transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess I’m here because things got… kind of intense. I’d barely even settled into my new apartment, and then suddenly I was saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, redesigning my whole portfolio. It felt like I had to fix my entire life all at once, like in one sprint.
Have you had any periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt like you had much more energy than usual, along with doing more activities than you normally would?

Yeah… earlier this month, I guess. I felt kind of wired, almost electric, and really upbeat for a bit. But then I’d get irritated fast—like snapping at a contractor, or my sister, over small delays. It felt like they were getting in my way, even though… I know that sounds a little much.
How long did that wired, upbeat feeling last? Was it most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week, or was it more off and on?
It’s been… kind of on and off since I moved into the apartment, so about a month. Not sure I’d say it was exactly every day the whole day, but the whole pattern has been there since then.
Can you clarify if there was a specific period when you felt this way most of the day, nearly every day, for at least one week straight?
I don’t know if I can pin it down that neatly. It’s more like… since I moved into the apartment, about a month ago, the whole intense up-and-down thing has been going on.

Can you think of a time when you felt unusually upbeat or high, with so much energy that you were doing a lot more than usual—like taking on big projects or not needing much sleep—for at least a whole week without that feeling letting up?
I don’t know if I can separate it into one clean week like that. It’s more that this whole intense up-and-down pattern has been going on since I moved into the apartment, about a month ago.
Can you think of a specific time in the past month when you felt unusually high, upbeat, or irritable for at least a full week straight, even if it was just during certain parts of the day?

Earlier this month, yeah… there was a stretch like that, I guess. I felt kind of electric, really upbeat at times, and then I’d get irritated fast—like snapping at a contractor or my sister over small delays. It felt bigger than it should’ve.
Can you tell me if there was a specific time when you felt unusually high, upbeat, or irritable for at least seven days in a row, even if it was just part of each day?

Yeah… earlier this month, I think. It wasn’t constant every second, but for days I felt kind of electric—really upbeat—and then I’d flip and get irritated over small stuff, like with a contractor or my sister. It felt… more intense than normal.
Can you tell me if the stretch of time when you felt electric, really upbeat, or irritable earlier this month lasted for at least 7 days in a row, even if it came and went during the day?

I mean… yes, I think so. It’s been kind of this whole up-and-down thing since I moved into the apartment, about a month ago. So that stretch earlier this month was definitely within that, and it felt like it went on for more than a week.
Can you confirm if the period when you felt electric, really upbeat, or irritable earlier this month lasted for at least 7 full days without a break?
I think so, yes. It’s hard to mark it exactly, but this whole intense up-and-down pattern has been going on since I moved into the apartment… about a month ago.
Can you confirm if the time when you felt electric, really upbeat, or irritable earlier this month had at least 7 full days in a row where you felt that way, without a break?
Yeah… I think so. I can’t pin it down perfectly, but this intense up-and-down thing has basically been going on since I moved into the apartment, about a month ago.
Can you confirm whether the time when you felt electric, really upbeat, or irritable earlier this month had at least 7 full days in a row where you felt that way, without any break at all?
I… I can’t say “without any break at all” for sure. I just know this whole intense up-and-down pattern has been going on since I moved into the apartment, about a month ago.
Can you confirm whether there was a period during that time when you felt electric, really upbeat, or irritable for at least 7 days straight, without any clear break at all?

I can’t honestly confirm the 7 days straight part. I just know earlier this month I was feeling… almost electric and really upbeat at times, and then I’d suddenly get irritated and snap at my contractor or my sister over tiny delays. Like it felt like they were blocking me on purpose.
Can you recall a specific time when you felt unusually high, upbeat, or irritable for at least 7 full days in a row without any noticeable break or relief from that feeling?

Not really a clean seven days, no. Earlier this month I did feel almost… electric, really upbeat for stretches, and then I’d get irritated fast—like snapping at my contractor or my sister over tiny delays. It felt like they were blocking me on purpose. But I can’t say it was seven full days without relief.
Can you recall a time when you felt unusually high, upbeat, or irritable for at least 4 full days in a row without any clear break?

I think… maybe, earlier this month. I felt kind of electric, really upbeat at points, and then I’d get irritated fast—like snapping at my contractor or my sister over little delays. It felt personal, like they were trying to block me. I’m not totally sure about the exact four full days, though.
Can you confirm whether there was a time earlier this month when you felt unusually upbeat, high, or irritable for at least 4 full days in a row without any clear break?

I can’t really confirm the full four days without a break. Earlier this month there was a stretch where I felt almost electric, upbeat, and then I’d suddenly snap at my contractor or my sister over tiny delays… like they were trying to block me.
Can you think of a specific time earlier this month when you felt unusually upbeat, high, or irritable for at least 4 full days in a row, without any clear break in between?

I mean… the closest was earlier this month. I felt kind of electric, like really upbeat, and then I’d get irritated really fast. I snapped at my contractor and my sister over small delays, like they were doing it to block me. I don’t know if I can pin down the exact four days, though.
Can you think of a specific time earlier this month when you felt unusually upbeat, high, or irritable for at least 4 full days in a row, without any clear break in between?

I’m not sure I can give you exact dates. Earlier this month there was a stretch where I felt almost electric—upbeat, but also really easily irritated. I snapped at my contractor and my sister over small delays, like they were personally trying to block me.
Can you think of a time when you felt unusually upbeat or high, along with doing a lot more activities or projects than usual, that lasted for at least four days in a row?

Yeah… I guess that fits more than just the “up” feeling. I’d just moved, and I went from barely getting settled to suddenly saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and trying to redesign my whole portfolio. It felt like I needed to fix everything at once, like in one sprint.

Can you confirm whether the time earlier this month when you felt electric and upbeat, along with taking on extra projects and mentoring, represented a noticeable change from how you usually feel and act, and lasted for at least 4 days in a row?

Yes… it was definitely different from my usual. I’d been barely getting settled into my new apartment, and then suddenly I was saying yes to mentoring, taking extra client prototypes, trying to redo my whole portfolio. It felt like I had to fix everything at once. And yeah, it went on for at least four days.
Did the time when you felt electric and upbeat, along with taking on extra projects and mentoring, cause any problems in your relationships or work?

Yeah… it did cause some problems. I missed a design review, which isn’t really like me. And I’ve kind of been avoiding friends and family since then because I feel embarrassed about how scattered and unreliable I must’ve seemed.
